business_problem: BT Group needed a secure, centrally governed way to scale generative AI beyond ad hoc experimentation, with cost control, privacy, prompt security, model monitoring, and flexibility to use multiple LLM providers without lock-in.
solution_summary: BT Group’s Digital Unit built the internal GenAI Gateway with AWS as a shared generative AI enablement layer for business teams and engineers. The platform is deployed on AWS and exposed through secure APIs inside BT Group’s modular digital architecture so applications can access approved LLM capabilities through one controlled entry point instead of standing up separate model stacks. GenAI Gateway uses Amazon Bedrock to provide access to multiple foundation model providers through a single API and Amazon SageMaker to support machine learning operations for BT’s use cases. The platform adds prompt security, chat history, enterprise search, per-use-case FinOps billing, and access to multiple corporate data sources. BT also applies central privacy controls such as separate tenants per use case, PII filters, UK data location, and isolation between trained models. Guardrails filter unsafe or out-of-scope prompts, while BT’s data fabric platform enforces data governance, access control, and data sovereignty restrictions.

data_flow: Users and internal applications call GenAI Gateway through secure APIs. The gateway applies prompt security, privacy controls, tenancy separation, PII filtering, guardrails, and budget controls, then routes requests to foundation models accessed via Amazon Bedrock and AI tooling in Amazon SageMaker. Corporate data sources and enterprise search features are brought into the workflow, and BT’s data fabric governs policy enforcement, access, and sovereignty constraints before responses are returned to business use cases.
integration_points: Secure internal APIs in BT Group's modular digital architecture
Foundation model providers accessed through Amazon Bedrock, including Anthropic, Cohere, Meta, Mistral AI, Stability AI, AI21 Labs, and Amazon

business_outcome: BT Group launched GenAI Gateway into live beta use, giving the company a centralized platform for safe, flexible generative AI adoption at scale. The first use cases include summarizing Openreach engineering notes to simplify processes and boost productivity, plus contract analysis for business, legal, and procurement teams.
